title: Sequential Retrieval in Dense Associative Memory: Asymptotic Dynamics and Storage Capacity
authors: Mao Mishima, Ayaka Sakata, Kazushi Mimura
abstract: We study the retrieval dynamics of an $n$-body asymmetric dense associative memory model, in which sequential retrieval is implemented by shifting one pattern index in the higher-order Hebbian interaction. The model exhibits sequential retrieval of the stored patterns, and the retrieval state corresponds to a stable limit-cycle attractor. The storage capacity is defined as the maximum loading rate for which this limit cycle remains stable. Using generating functional analysis, we derive the dynamical equations describing the sequential retrieval state. The generating functional analysis reveals that the retarded self-interaction term vanishes in the asymmetric model, and the resulting overlap dynamics is reproduced by an Amari-Maginu-type signal-to-noise analysis. Also, we find that for the interaction order $n\ge 3$, the normalized storage capacity decreases monotonically with increasing interaction order, in contrast to symmetric Modern Hopfield models.
summary: This paper analyzes a modified, asymmetric Hopfield-type memory model designed to exhibit sequential pattern retrieval. Using advanced techniques like Generating Functional Analysis, the authors derive the dynamics of the system's order parameters. They establish that the memory's capacity scales differently with interaction order compared to standard symmetric models, providing theoretical bounds for pattern storage.
main_problem: The study focuses on the retrieval dynamics and storage capacity of an $n$-body asymmetric dense associative memory model, specifically investigating sequential pattern retrieval.
main_result: The asymmetric coupling induces sequential retrieval characterized by a stable limit-cycle attractor, and the normalized storage capacity decreases monotonically with increasing interaction order $n$ for $n \ge 3$.
method: The analysis employs Generating Functional Analysis (GFA) to derive the dynamical equations, followed by saddle-point approximations to characterize the order parameters in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The model is an $n$-body asymmetric dense associative memory, generalizing the Hopfield model by shifting one pattern index in the higher-order interaction tensor, leading to sequential pattern recall.
key_observables: Overlap parameters ($m(t), q(t,t'), K(t,t')$), the critical retrieval overlap ($m_c$), and the storage capacity ($\alpha'_c$ or $M_{	ext{ret}}^c$).
important_parameters: Interaction order ($n$), system size ($N$), loading rate ($\alpha$), and the time evolution parameter $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$) and utilizes the saddle-point approximation on the generating functional. It also assumes sequential retrieval occurs.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate sequential retrieval processes at varying loading rates ($\alpha'$) and show the dependence of the retrieval threshold ($\alpha_{c,n}'$) and critical overlap ($m_c$) on the interaction order $n$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the dynamics using GFA, deriving saddle-point equations for order parameters. It analyzes the absence of retarded self-interaction in the asymmetric case and derives asymptotic scaling laws for the critical capacity as $n$ increases.
why_interesting: The rigorous theoretical analysis of pattern dynamics in associative memories, especially the derivation of limit-cycle attractors and capacity scaling laws, provides deep insights into non-equilibrium dynamics relevant to complex quantum systems.
